html:
The Astrakhan Khanate was a Tatar state at the mouth of the Volga, one of the successors of the Golden Horde, from the 1460s to 1556. It is on the map for 1530.

Its khans descended from Jochi, the eldest son of Genghis Khan. Its capital, Xacitarxan, known in Russian as Astrakhan, sat on the Volga delta, on the trade route between Russia, the Caspian Sea, Persia and Central Asia. The khanate was small and weak, pushed around by the Crimean Khanate, the Nogai Horde of the steppe and the growing power of Moscow.

After Ivan the Terrible took the Kazan Khanate in 1552, his armies went down the Volga and took Astrakhan in 1556. Russia now held the whole Volga, from its sources to the Caspian, and could trade and expand south and east; see Tsardom of Muscovy.
